items: Achan coveted a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels' weight (Joshua 7:21) when they went to war with Ai after God had warned them not to take any accursed thing.
He brought defeat to Israel (Joshua 7:5); he admitted to having sinned (Joshua 7:20) and was stoned to death (Joshua 7:25).

Gehazi, Elisha’s servant, ran greedily after Naaman and lied to him because he coveted the gifts Naaman brought for His master, which he rejected (2 Kings 5:21-22). Gehazi and his generation got Naaman’s leprosy (2 Kings 5:26-27).

King David coveted Uriah’s wife, Bathsheba, and committed adultery with her (2 Samuel 11:2-4). That singular act led him to become a murderer because he initiated Uriah’s death (2Samuel 11:15, 24); he lost the child born by Bathsheba (2 Samuel 12:15-18), and God swore that the sword shall never depart from David’s house (2 Samuel 12:9-12).

King Ahab longed for Naboth’s vineyard; the latter refused, and it led to his death (1 Kings 21:1-3; 13). God took the kingship lineage from Ahab and, at the same time, pronounced a death sentence upon him and his family (1 Kings 21:19-22).
